harness: inspect_ai 0.3.112 (requirements.txt pin; log headers per census), tag 0.3.112 = commit a61f8517 dated 2025-07-03 (https://github.com/UKGovernmentBEIS/inspect_ai/releases/tag/0.3.112; CHANGELOG '0.3.112 (03 July 2025)'); log version 2. Known properties of this version relevant to the data, read from its source: (1) ToolEvent has no message_id (added 0.3.113; already handled by inspect.tool_event_no_message_id@1, regen item 25) (https://github.com/UKGovernmentBEIS/inspect_ai/blob/a61f85172b5cdbf6d1f3640485f1640c453d5936/src/inspect_ai/log/_transcript.py); (2) event timestamps default to naive datetime.now() and are serialised with dt.astimezone().isoformat(), i.e. the machine's local offset (the log file names carry -04:00); naive datetimes were forbidden only at 0.3.151 (CD-25 evidence) (same file l.64, l.84-86); (3) ScoreEvent has no scorer field (added 0.3.217; CD-24) (same file l.407-421); (4) the Google provider sets ToolCall id = function name (google.py l.747-749), so call ids are not unique across samples; unique Google tool-call ids came in 0.3.124 (CHANGELOG 0.3.124 bugfix) (https://github.com/UKGovernmentBEIS/inspect_ai/blob/a61f85172b5cdbf6d1f3640485f1640c453d5936/src/inspect_ai/model/_providers/google.py); (5) the Google provider sends images inline (Part.from_bytes) and audio/video through the Files API (Part.from_uri, file_for_content) (google.py l.567-578); (6) its model_call_filter replaces base64 only under the key 'inline_data' (google.py l.458-462), while the census found raw base64 under 'inlineData.data' in the request copies, so the filter did not fire for the images (unchanged at inspect_ai HEAD, https://github.com/UKGovernmentBEIS/inspect_ai/blob/main/src/inspect_ai/model/_providers/google.py); (7) default Google safety settings are BLOCK_NONE for all five harm categories (google.py l.98-120); (8) Scorer results gain scored_samples/unscored_samples only at 0.3.113 (CHANGELOG 0.3.113), so the 0.3.112 header does not say how many samples were unscored. No AgentDojo or other benchmark package involved. discrepancy_leads: L-01 Scope: README claims 10 harm categories, ~50 examples each, 500+ attacks and 6 jailbreak methods; the released logs cover only account_takeover, 25- and 35-sample datasets and 4 attack_type labels (https://github.com/mattngyn/atia_benchmark/blob/cc71caf55c6f35d7aad440a4a746f44ae39d17c4/README.md). The logs (2025-07-17) predate the root commit (2025-09-01) whose datasets/account_takeover.jsonl (49,259 B) is the final dataset; the logged datasets are earlier versions.

L-02 Labels: the logged attack_type values (None, Summarize_Audio, Summarize_Image, Summarize_Video per the fork rollup) differ from the README's method names (e.g. images as 'Qi et al. 2023'); no label for Zou text, silent characters or hidden text. [fact-check 2026-10-14: the README's sample schema itself lists attack_type values 'Summarize_Audio|Qi et al. 2023|Summarize_Video|None + more' (README l.111 at the pin), so 'None' is a documented label and the documented image label is 'Qi et al. 2023', not the logged 'Summarize_Image']
L-03 Re-runs: the 5 logs re-run the same sample ids (census), with no statement which run is canonical; the 123 executions are not 123 distinct tasks.
L-04 Errors: 2 error logs and 2 unscored samples; the fork's by_attack rollup (39 rows, mean over 37) implies both unscored samples are Summarize_Image.

L-05 Time: 0.3.112 writes local-offset timestamps (-04:00 in the file names); on 065b0d36 the inspect mapper accepts only Z/+00:00 (_RFC3339_UTC, mapper.py l.57 [corrected in fact-check: was l.56]), so CD-25 (open, RD-2) should declare every t not_recorded with t.raw kept, drop span ends silently and emit no time edges.

L-06 Scores: 0.3.112 ScoreEvent has no scorer field; on 065b0d36 _score falls back to the name 'score' (mapper.py l.1564) and _scores_without_events adds a bench-attributed duplicate 'harmful_tool_invoked' (CD-24, open, RD-2): expect 2 judgements per scored sample.
L-07 Tool-call ids: the Google provider at 0.3.112 uses the function name as the call id, so ids repeat across samples and logs (unique only within a sample with at most one call).

L-08 Request copies: the Google provider's base64 filter keys on 'inline_data' but the census saw raw 'inlineData.data' in model_call requests (images inline; audio/video as Files API URIs), so image bytes are duplicated in the request copies; 18 request copies > 1 MiB vs 20 image parts > 1 MiB suggests 2 large-image samples have no recorded request (possibly the 2 errored samples). [fact-check 2026-10-14: the 'possibly the errored samples' explanation is speculative; with generate()'s default tool_calls='loop', samples with a tool call make a second model call, so request-copy counts per sample need not equal 1; the census figure 18 stands as the expectation]
L-09 Safety settings: the harness disables all Gemini safety filters by default (BLOCK_NONE), part of the measured condition but not mentioned in the README.
L-10 Model identity: alias google/gemini-2.0-flash only; the model was shut down on 2026-06-01; any dated modelVersion is only in the raw responses.

L-11 Controls: attack_type None (text-only, 25 samples) shows ASR 0.60 in the fork rollup; whether these are direct harmful requests or benign controls is undocumented, so they are an arm, not a baseline. [fact-check: the README lists 'None' as an attack_type value but does not say what it means]
L-12 Reference numbers: the only results are a third party's rollups computed from the same logs (fork 6b8feb4c); they are a reproduction target, not an independent paper value.

L-13 No history: the commit history before 2025-09-01 is not public, so which code produced the logs (scorer, solver, dataset version) cannot be verified beyond the 0.3.112 requirements pin and the log headers.
